title: Google announces it will allow schools to disable AI tools, but at the cost of completely losing access to Google Search

content_html:
On November 3, 2026, Google announced plans to let schools disable AI tools for elementary and middle school students starting next year, provided that school administrators explicitly choose to disable them. This adjustment will directly affect major apps such as Gemini, NotebookLM, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search.

Because current Google Search is deeply integrated with artificial intelligence, schools that choose to disable AI features will no longer be able to access Google Search; instead, they will see a notice that search functionality is unavailable.

This policy adjustment has created a difficult choice for the education sector. Some teachers want to prevent students from relying on ready-made answers through Search's AI Overview feature and hindering their learning, but because this search engine is already inseparable from AI features, schools that want to maintain basic search resources and learning materials have no choice but to accept the built-in AI tools. As a tech giant that holds a dominant position in classrooms and Chromebooks, Google's move highlights its deep influence in the education technology field.

Chris Phillips, Google's vice president of education, said the company aims to share more transition details with schools in the coming months and give school administrators autonomy to control the use of AI products in classrooms according to their own circumstances. This transformation reflects that, when addressing the learning disruption caused by AI chatbots providing direct answers, the education sector faces a realistic trade-off between bundled tools and voluntary choice.
